title: Journal intelligence dataset: acceptance rates, review times and desk-rejection rates for 57 journals, with per-figure evidence typing
description:
Acceptance rates, review timelines, desk-rejection rates and submission limits for 57 journals across 23 publishers and 17 fields.

The distinguishing feature is provenance. Every volatile figure carries an evidence type (official, reported, estimated), so a reuser can tell measurement from inference before citing it.

That typing is also the main finding. None of the 57 desk-rejection rates is officially published: all 57 are estimates. Only 4 of 57 acceptance rates are reported by any credible source, and none are official. Only 1 review time is official. The data researchers are routinely told to use when choosing a journal is, for the most part, not published by the journals.

Contents. CSV (26 columns, display strings) and JSON (29 fields, adding numeric day counts and array fields that the CSV flattens; prefer the JSON for analysis). Both carry version tag 2026.03.30-mvp1.

Read the estimated columns as inference, not measurement. Citing a specific estimated acceptance rate as a fact about that journal is a misuse of this dataset. Four further columns (difficulty score, difficulty band, primary fit signal, primary rejection reason) are Manusights editorial judgments drawn from pre-submission review work, not third-party data; treat them as opinion with a stated basis.

Coverage. Selection favoured journals researchers most often ask us about, which skews toward high-profile venues. 57 journals is a starting panel, not a census, and not a representative sample of the literature.

Corrections welcome: a publisher-stated figure will replace an estimate in the next version, with its type upgraded to official.
